annual_report.business: Jindal Drilling and Industries Limited operates jack-up rigs, directional drilling equipment, and mud logging services for offshore and onshore oil and gas exploration, primarily in India.
key_risks: Customer concentration risk — substantially the whole of the Company's revenue is derived from a single customer.
Contract renewal and re-tendering risk — charters are awarded for fixed terms and are subject to competitive re-tender on expiry.
Day-rate risk — day rates are fixed for the contract term, so cost inflation during the term cannot be passed on.

Geopolitical and supply chain risk — situation in the Middle East, including disruption to shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, affects movement of rigs, equipment and spares, insurance costs and mobilisation timelines.
Asset and operational risk — drilling operations are inherently hazardous and equipment-intensive.
Human resource risk — the availability and retention of qualified offshore crew is critical to operations.
Currency risk — a portion of the Company's revenues and costs are denominated in US dollars, exposing it to exchange rate movements.
Regulatory and compliance risk — the Company is subject to an extensive framework of maritime, environmental, safety and taxation regulation.
